_README: The squad the agent reasons about. Until a gameweek's deadline has
passed this is maintained by hand, because FPL keeps a team private
until then. Once a deadline passes, squad.py rewrites squad/my_lineup/
bank below automatically from the public API (see PLAN.md section 5b)
-- this file stops needing screenshots from that point on.
team_id is intentionally NEVER set here, and never will be -- this file
is committed to a public repo, and the FPL entry API returns the
manager's real first/last name alongside the team data. It lives ONLY
in the FPL_TEAM_ID GitHub Actions secret (Settings -> Secrets and
variables -> Actions), the same place RESEND_API_KEY lives.
Players are listed by FPL web_name, with team where the name is
ambiguous (there are two Hughes).
my_lineup (optional): your OWN captain/bench choice from the FPL app,
so the dashboard can show what you actually set instead of guessing.
Leave it null and the dashboard just lists your 15 with no captain or
bench guessed for you. Fill it in like:
"my_lineup": {"captain": "Haaland", "vice_captain": "B.Fernandes",
"bench": ["Steele", "O'Shea", "Wilson", "Solanke"]}
(bench must be exactly 4 names, exactly one of them your reserve
goalkeeper -- his order in the list doesn't matter, the dashboard always
draws him first, matching the FPL app; the other three render in the
order given). Once FPL_TEAM_ID is set, squad.py keeps this filled in
automatically and it stops needing to be entered by hand.
team_id_note: Deliberately not stored here -- see _README. Set FPL_TEAM_ID as a GitHub secret instead.
